A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, objectives, numerical examples, and appendices A and B. Their complete text, equations, and figures support comparison, including the added appendix subsection in v3.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figure 2 report original numerical trajectories and convergence curves for gradient descent on an anisotropic two-dimensional Gaussian proximal problem.

after.justification: Section 5 and Figure 2 retain the original Gaussian numerical experiment and its computed trajectories and convergence curves.

M1.justification: With alpha_k still equal to 1/(k+2), v3 changes the core update from alpha_k MMSE+(1-alpha_k)y to (1-alpha_k)MMSE+alpha_k y. Algorithm 1 also replaces the fixed observation y in each inner update with the current post-gradient point. These substantive corrections change the stated iterates and proximal target, aligning the procedure with the gradient formulation already analyzed in v1.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic two-dimensional Gaussian proximal problem. The approximate-score extension in v3 is theoretical; it adds no dataset, trained-denoiser evaluation, or empirical test scenario.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains the same comparison against naive gradient descent on the unsmoothed objective. The added Xu et al. citation does not introduce an evaluated baseline.

E3.justification: The numerical example retains the same covariance construction, condition number of 500, baseline step size of 0.8/L_F, and distance-to-proximal-point metric. The evaluated smoothed-gradient schedule is unchanged; no new experimental protocol is reported.

E4.justification: Section 3.3 and new Appendix A.3 add an analytical sensitivity assessment of uniformly bounded score-approximation errors, quantifying their contribution to residual proximal error. This is theoretical error analysis, not a new empirical robustness experiment or ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for the numerical example. The new deterministic score-error bound does not change statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Figures 1 and 2 retain the same contours, trajectories, and convergence curves. Both report poor progress for unsmoothed gradient descent and approximately 1/k decay for the smoothed procedure; no empirical result entries are added or changed.

T1.justification: New Proposition 6 and its proof in Appendix A.3 extend the central convergence analysis to uniformly bounded score errors, adding sqrt(3/2) times tau times xi to the original error bound. There are also local mathematical revisions, including Proposition 4's covariance scaling. The existing Gaussian, affine-subspace, and Appendix B results are retained after renumbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a smoothed-gradient interpretation, convergence to the true proximal operator under the stated regularity assumptions, and integration into approximate proximal gradient descent for MAP estimation.

C2.justification: v3 newly discusses applicability to approximate learned scores and an O(xi) residual-error neighborhood. Its wording about convergence to a point is stronger than Proposition 6's distance bound alone establishes. The existing limitations concerning log-concavity and more general manifold-supported priors remain.

D1.justification: The numerical-example setup and implementation disclosures are unchanged. Neither version supplies additional code or data access, hardware, training details, or reproducibility resources.

R1.justification: v3 adds Xu et al. (2020), 'Provable convergence of plug-and-play priors with MMSE denoisers,' to the related-work discussion and bibliography. The broader positioning against PnP, conditional diffusion, and flow-based approaches remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes outer and inner iteration notation, makes some assumption references explicit, expands an intermediate proof step, and inserts the approximate-score subsection. Most prose and the main section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adopts conference formatting with different typography, heading sizes, spacing, and figure scaling, plus a NeurIPS footer. Both figures retain their panels, axes, legends, and underlying content; no new figure or results table appears.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves an important mismatch between the published averaging recursion and Algorithm 1 and the proximal-gradient procedure analyzed in the proofs. Correcting both the weights and the inner proximal anchor substantially improves correctness and implementability. Proposition 6 also supplies an explicit guarantee for approximate scores. Its surrounding prose overstates convergence to a single point, but this qualification does not outweigh the central corrections and theoretical extension; empirical evidence remains unchanged.
